Postdoctoral Research Associate in Mathematical Physics (Senior Research Associate)

School Of Physics And Astronomy
Location:  Bailrigg, Lancaster, UK
Salary:   £40,704 to £46,970 (Full time, indefinite with end date)
Closing Date:   Tuesday 15 December 2026
Interview Date:   Friday 15 January 2027
Reference:  1286-26

Lancaster University’s School of Physics and Astronomy is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate (Senior Research Associate) as part of the John Templeton Foundation award “Open Quantum Systems  and the Causal Structure of Reality”. 

The Open Systems collaboration will apply formal, physical and conceptional innovations from the study of open quantum systems to systems without fixed causal structure. Quantum models of the universe feature non-fixed causal structure in terms of dynamical and, in some cases, emergent spacetime structure. Quantum cosmology offers the most general and challenging arena for the open systems approach to physics and metaphysics, since the standard assumption is that the universe is subject to closed quantum dynamics. Fundamental reality is standardly understood by philosophers and scientists to be whatever provides the basis for everything.

The Postdoctoral Research Associate will lead their own research program, and be encouraged to work in this area on issues regarding general relativity and cosmology contributing to questions of the role of scale in general relativity, the emergence of temporal structure, the use of quantum reference frames or other related issues. 

The Postdoctoral Research Associate post is full time, funded for 24 months from 1st July 2027. In conjunction with the standard application process, please upload a CV and also a writing sample of either a) your best published work or b) single thesis chapter (in the latter case, 30 pages maximum inclusive of references) with your application.

If you have any queries regarding this position, please contact David Sloan at d.sloan@lancaster.ac.uk

Research Technician Plant Sciences

Lancaster Environment Centre
Location:  Bailrigg, Lancaster, UK
Salary:   £27,241 to £30,986 (Full-Time/Fixed-Term)
Closing Date:   Sunday 06 December 2026
Interview Date:   To be confirmed
Reference:  1242-26

Lancaster Environment Centre at Lancaster University is seeking to appoint a Research Technician. This role is available for a period of 5 months starting 1 December 2026

 This role will provide essential support to the department’s research activities. This project offers an opportunity for you to directly impact the development of materials for sustainable agriculture (particularly how their properties may influence their interactions with plants) in collaboration with an industry partner. You will apply plant growth regulators developed by the University’s Chemistry department, and evaluate their biological effects which may include imposing defined plant stress treatments. 

ABOUT YOU

The successful candidate will:

Have experience in working with plants (propagation, growth, maintenance and routine measurements of plant performance)
Be able to demonstrate competent knowledge of health and safety and have experience of implementing safe systems and controls
Have experience of working in a plant science laboratory using a range of plant science related skills

THE BENEFITS OF THE ROLE

Generous holiday leave - 25 days (pro-rata) annual leave plus University closure days and bank holidays.
Access to employee pension scheme, and annual flexible benefits scheme.
We are committed to promoting Equality, Diversity and Inclusion across the Faculty, and supporting family-friendly and flexible working policies on an individual basis. The Department holds an Athena Swan Silver Award, which recognises and celebrates good employment practice undertaken to address gender equality in Higher Education and research.  

Lancaster Environment Centre: Our vision is to work across disciplines, and societal and national boundaries, to address the major environmental challenges facing the world. As one of the world’s largest centres for environmental research, our academic expertise spans the natural and social sciences, offering balanced perspectives on what are complex societal challenges. Our teaching programmes and research reflect this diversity, operating at the crucial interface between the environment and society. Further information about the Department is available at: https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/lec/ 

Lancaster University is highly ranked (10th overall in the UK Complete University Guide 2027; 15th overall in the UK and named University of the Year in the Northwest in the Times / Sunday Times Good University Guide 2026); and 14th overall in the UK in the Guardian University Guide 2026). It was awarded the Times International University of the Year in 2020 and University of the Year in 2018, and holds a Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF) Gold rating. The University’s campus is located in 560 acres of beautiful parkland on the edge of the small but vibrant city of Lancaster.

Informal enquiries are welcome and should be addressed to Prof. Ian Dodd i.dodd@lancaster.ac.uk and Dr John hardy, j.g.hardy@lancaster.ac.uk 

Please upload a one page cover letter with your application.

postings.advert_text:
Research Technician in Virology

Are you an early career researcher looking for a challenge? Do you have a background in cell biology or virology? Do you want to further your career in one of the UK’s leading research-intensive Universities?

We have a vacancy for a virologist to study the host-pathogen interactions of a group of viruses known as the bunyaviruses. This appointment is part of an international collaboration involving scientists working in virology, immunology, structural biology, and cutting-edge image analysis. We seek to understand the formation of viral factories by bunyaviruses within host cells at the molecular and atomic level. The appointment will be for 60 months.

You should have an undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in a biological science microbiology, biochemistry, or equivalent experience, with practical experience of mammalian cell biology or virology. The successful candidate will join the thriving research environment within the Faculty of Health and Life Sciences and have the opportunity to use and gain experience of new state-of-the-art research facilities in cell biology, molecular virology and cell imaging. The successful applicant will have the opportunity to register for a part-time PhD.

What we offer in return

• 26 days’ holiday plus approx. 16 Bank Holidays/days that the University is closed by custom (including Christmas) – that’s 42 days a year!

• Generous pension scheme options plus life assurance

• Health and Wellbeing: discounted staff membership options at The Edge, our state-of-the-art Campus gym, with pool, sauna, climbing wall, cycle circuit, and sports halls

• Personal Development: Access to courses run by our Organisational Development & Professional Learning team. All FMH staff are entitled to ten days’ staff development per year (pro rata). Please speak to your Line Manager about how you can utilise these

• Access to on-site childcare, shopping discounts and travel schemes are also available

And much more !

If you are looking for a role that will challenge and reward you, please apply today.

To explore the post further or for any queries you may have, please contact: 

Dr John N. Barr, Associate Professor

Tel: +44 (0)113 343 8069

Email: j.n.barr@leeds.ac.uk

Please note that this role is not eligible for Skilled Worker visa sponsorship. Information on other visa options is available via the Government’s Work in the UK page.

Postdoctoral Researcher - School of Communication & Design (1FTE FTC)
DATE ADVERTISED

19 November 2026

CLOSING DATE

13 December 2026

SCHOOL/AREA

School of Communication & Design

PROGRAMME/​DEPARTMENT

Design Research Projects

REQUIRED HOURS

Full Time

SITE

Battersea, London, United Kingdom

SALARY

£45,638 - £50,575 per annum

Fixed Term from February 2027 for 10 months

Postdoctoral Researcher

1.0 FTE | Fixed-term for 10 months | Starting February 2027

The Royal College of Art, the world's leading university of art and design, is seeking an ambitious and innovative Postdoctoral Researcher to join an exciting BBSRC-funded research project exploring the development of programmable, 3D-printed biomaterial environments.

Working in collaboration with Imperial College London and CABI, this interdisciplinary project aims to develop new hydrogel-based materials that enable researchers to investigate how plants and microorganisms interact within carefully controlled, engineered environments.

The project brings together expertise in biomaterials, digital manufacturing and applied microbiology to create a reproducible experimental platform with potential applications in agricultural biotechnology and the development of more resilient biological systems.

About the role

Based at the RCA, you will lead experimental research into the formulation, development and characterisation of 3D-printable hydrogel-based biomaterials. You will investigate material compositions, fabrication processes and printing parameters, exploring how their physical and chemical properties influence biological compatibility and performance.

You will also undertake microbial culture experiments at the RCA and CABI, investigating microbial growth, viability and interactions within engineered biomaterial environments.

Working closely with colleagues across all three partner organisations, you will contribute to experimental design, data analysis and validation of the research platform. You will also play an important role in disseminating findings through scientific publications, presentations and other research outputs.

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to innovative, interdisciplinary research at the intersection of materials science, digital fabrication and microbiology.

About you

You will have a background in biomaterials, materials science, bioengineering, biotechnology, additive manufacturing or a closely related discipline, supported by a PhD, equivalent professional experience, or a Master's degree alongside significant relevant research experience.

You will bring practical experience in developing and characterising biomaterials, particularly hydrogels or polymer-based materials, alongside experience of extrusion-based 3D printing or bioprinting.

You will also have hands-on experience of microbial culture techniques, including aseptic handling and assessing microbial growth or viability, as well as the ability to design and deliver reproducible laboratory experiments and analyse quantitative data.

We are looking for someone who can work independently, troubleshoot experimental challenges and contribute effectively to a collaborative, interdisciplinary research team. You will have strong written and verbal communication skills, experience of producing research outputs and a commitment to high standards of research integrity and practice.

Experience of computational design, Python or MATLAB programming, hydrogel rheology, microscopy or working with external research partners would be advantageous.

Why join the RCA?

The Royal College of Art offers a unique environment for interdisciplinary research, bringing together creative practice, scientific innovation and technological development. You will have the opportunity to work with leading research partners and contribute to a collaborative project addressing important challenges in agricultural biotechnology.

If you are excited by the opportunity to combine materials innovation, digital manufacturing and biological research, we would love to hear from you.

Please see Information pack for more details.

Closing for applications at 11.59pm on Sunday 13th December 2026
